statement: A quasi-unipotent rational cyclic germ determines a unique additive one-parameter group; it agrees only after finite index.
notes: Full logarithm/exponential proof; -1 in Gm distinguishes germ from full homomorphism.

statement: Integral extension is equivalent to divided-power integrality over a torsion-free ring; every fibrewise quasi-unipotent section of a closed finitely presented linear group has a positive power on Ga.
notes: LM1 proofs reopened and checked; constructible compactness, Cayley–Hamilton, binomial dilation and Vandermonde torsion killing reproduced.

statement: Fibrewise unipotence alone does not imply an undilated integral additive parameter.
notes: Rank-five weighted shift (1,2,3,2); exact X^4/4!=E15/2; all geometric fibres explicitly verified.

statement: Smooth additive schematic closure does not imply a primitive map from some positive-index subgroup of the original cyclic lattice.
notes: Counterexample k↦2k into Ga_Z. Primitive parameter exists but does not lie in the original integral image. Actual scans inspected.

statement: Additive subgroups whose tangent images span the Lie algebra generate a smooth finite-presentation group with connected fibres as an etale sheaf.
notes: Additional component representatives needed without connected fibres; proof by a smooth multiplication map and open subgroup.

statement: Explicit torus and four-puncture twists on chosen Malcev classes 1 and 2 have the stated logarithms and Magnus integral denominators at 2 and 3.
manuscript_passages: C4 scans 210–221; explicitly chosen auxiliary approximations
notes: Torus class-two Magnus action requires power 2; sphere separating twist needs no dilation. These are not a canonical first/second §52 tower.

statement: Free-word braid, reflection and centre-square identities hold on nilpotent classes 1–4; all nilpotent quotients of B3 itself are cyclic.
manuscript_passages: C4 scan 231, fol. 763, location corrected to scans 234–237, fols. 764′–766
notes: Exact reduced-word checks followed by independent Magnus matrices of dimensions 3,7,15,31.

statement: Over Z/p^e, a section of any group scheme whose special-fibre reduction has finite order has finite order; the positive-power claim follows for quasi-unipotent sections.
manuscript_passages: C4 scans 211–213; LM1 E.11 test base Z/4
notes: No affine or linear assumption; successive square-zero identity kernels have exponent p. This resolves the stated Z/4 test, not every nonlinear base.

statement: Full smooth integral model existence and the remaining general nonlinear positive-power assertion are not established in this package.
notes: D.11 resolves the nonlinear dual-number test; general positive-dimensional bases and extra integral-model conditions remain unresolved.

statement: Discrete relations and agreement on integer sections do not suffice for the proposed presentation of the integral group sheaf.
notes: Ga² with primitive axes: target Heisenberg sheaf in characteristic p and additive t^p−t maps satisfy all integer relations but have nonzero cross commutator.

statement: For every separated finite-presentation group scheme over characteristic-zero dual numbers, a section with unipotent reduction lies on a unique additive subgroup; quasi-unipotent reduction is handled after a positive power.
manuscript_passages: C4 scans 210–213, §52.3; nonlinear test after LM1
notes: Weil restriction is represented by a finite-type field group even without flatness; its reduction kernel is a vector group; preimage of cyclic unipotent closure is unipotent. Full proof of nonflat image correction.
